hot.title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
hot.summary: Vector Policy Optimization (VPO) trains large language models to generate diverse candidate solutions by leveraging vector-valued reward structures and stochastic scalarization. This method consistently achieves higher best@k scores and maintains greater reward-space diversity compared to scalar reinforcement learning baselines across multiple domains, significantly enhancing performance in test-time search applications.

hot.title: Generative Recursive Reasoning
hot.summary: Researchers from KAIST, Mila, New York University, and Université de Montréal introduced Generative Recursive Reasoning Models (GRAM), a framework that injects stochasticity into recursive neural networks to enable multi-hypothesis exploration and generative capabilities. GRAM achieves improved performance on complex structured reasoning and multi-solution constraint satisfaction problems, outperforming deterministic recursive baselines and demonstrating high-quality unconditional generation of diverse data.

hot.title: Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search
hot.summary: Google DeepMind, Aarhus University, and Google researchers developed AlphaProof Nexus, an AI-driven formal proof search framework that autonomously resolved several open, research-level problems in mathematics by integrating large language models with the Lean proof assistant. The system successfully generated mechanically verifiable proofs for long-standing conjectures in various mathematical domains, addressing the unreliability of natural language AI in complex mathematical reasoning.

hot.title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
hot.summary: Gated DeltaNet-2, developed by researchers at NVIDIA, enhances linear recurrent attention models by decoupling memory erase and write operations through distinct channel-wise gates. This refined approach improves performance across language modeling, common-sense reasoning, and retrieval tasks, showing particular gains on long-context benchmarks requiring robust interference control.

hot.title: Memory-R2: Fair Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
hot.summary: Memory-R2 introduces a training framework that enhances credit assignment for long-horizon memory-augmented LLM agents in multi-session environments and jointly optimizes memory formation and evolution. The approach achieved an F1 score of 50.60 and BLEU-1 of 44.01 on the LoCoMo benchmark, outperforming previous baselines, and demonstrated strong generalization across various models and benchmarks.

hot.title: Equilibrium Reasoners: Learning Attractors Enables Scalable Reasoning
hot.summary: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University developed Equilibrium Reasoners (EqR), an iterative model framework that leverages task-conditioned attractors in latent space to achieve scalable and generalizable reasoning. EqR, trained with novel techniques, attained over 99% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme by adaptively scaling computational depth and breadth.

hot.title: WorldKV: Efficient World Memory with World Retrieval and Compression
hot.summary: WorldKV presents a training-free framework for autoregressive video world models, allowing them to sustain persistent and consistent explorable worlds over long durations while maintaining real-time inference speeds. It achieves this by selectively retrieving and compressing Key-Value (KV) cache chunks, matching or exceeding the memory fidelity of full KV-cache attention while doubling throughput.

hot.title: Code as Agent Harness
hot.summary: Researchers from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Meta, and Stanford University present a conceptual framework, "code as agent harness," repositioning code from an LLM output to an operational substrate enabling robust agent intelligence. This work systematizes how code facilitates agent reasoning, action, environment modeling, and verifiable long-horizon task execution through a three-layered taxonomy.

hot.title: Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents
hot.summary: Peking University researchers introduced LIFE-HARNESS, a method to enhance the performance of frozen large language model (LLM) agents by adapting their runtime interface rather than modifying model parameters. This approach achieved an average relative performance improvement of 88.5% across 18 diverse LLM backbones and seven deterministic agent environments, effectively transferring interventions evolved from one model to others.

hot.title: Tokenisation via Convex Relaxations
hot.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and Kensho Technologies developed ConvexTok, a tokenization algorithm that approximates a globally optimal solution by formulating tokenization as an Integer Program and relaxing it into a Linear Program. This method achieves compression rates within 1% of a provable theoretical optimum and improves Bits-per-Byte for language models compared to Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) at larger vocabulary sizes.

hot.title: Sensor2Sensor: Cross-Embodiment Sensor Conversion for Autonomous Driving
hot.summary: Waymo researchers introduce Sensor2Sensor, a generative framework that translates real-world monocular videos into high-fidelity, multi-modal autonomous vehicle sensor logs, including 360-degree camera views and LiDAR point clouds. This system, which employs 4D Gaussian Splatting for synthetic data generation and a multi-modal diffusion model, achieves superior fidelity and temporal stability in generated sensor data compared to baselines and generalizes effectively to diverse in-the-wild footage.

hot.title: The Log is the Agent: Event-Sourced Reactive Graphs for Auditable, Forkable Agentic Systems
hot.summary: Untapped Capital's ActiveGraph introduces an event-sourced, reactive graph runtime for LLM agents, re-architecting systems by making an append-only event log the primary source of truth for all agent activities and state. This architecture enables byte-deterministic replay, cheap forking for counterfactual analysis, and end-to-end lineage tracking, as demonstrated by a diligence pack example producing 671 events and 93 objects without explicit orchestration.

hot.title: Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
hot.summary: The Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model (PTRM) integrates inference-time stochasticity and a Q-head-based selection mechanism into deterministic Tiny Recursive Models (TRMs). This method improves reasoning accuracy on the PPBench golden set by 28.6 percentage points over standard TRMs, achieving higher performance than frontier LLMs at a much lower computational cost.

hot.title: Cambrian-P: Pose-Grounded Video Understanding
hot.summary: A model named Cambrian-P augments multimodal large language models for video understanding with explicit camera pose grounding, addressing limitations in spatial reasoning. This approach achieves a 4.5% accuracy improvement on VSI-Bench and records a minimal Absolute Trajectory Error of 0.078 on ScanNet for streaming pose estimation.

hot.title: Forecasting Scientific Progress with Artificial Intelligence
hot.summary: This research introduces CUSP, a multi-disciplinary benchmark, to evaluate AI's capacity for forecasting scientific progress under strict temporal knowledge constraints. The study reveals that frontier AI models exhibit systematic limitations, performing near chance on predicting the feasibility of scientific claims and struggling with precise timing, while showing some capability in mechanistic reasoning.

hot.title: AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration
hot.summary: UNC-Chapel Hill and collaborators introduce AutoResearchClaw, a multi-agent autonomous research pipeline designed to mimic the iterative and self-correcting nature of human scientific inquiry. The system achieves a 54.7% improvement in overall performance on the ARC-Bench compared to existing LLM agents, enhancing hypothesis quality, execution robustness, and verifiable reporting through structured debate, self-healing execution, and cross-run learning.

hot.title: MotiMotion: Motion-Controlled Video Generation with Visual Reasoning
hot.summary: A framework called MotiMotion enhances motion-controlled video generation by integrating visual reasoning and confidence-aware control, enabling the system to infer complex, physically plausible dynamics from sparse user trajectories. The approach demonstrates superior performance on the new MotiBench benchmark, achieving 0.302 in physical realism metrics, and a 97.9% human preference rate over MagicMotion and 81.4% over Wan-Move.

hot.title: HRM-Text: Efficient Pretraining Beyond Scaling
Action with Visual Primitives
hot.summary: The Action with Visual Primitives (AVP) framework introduces an end-to-end Vision-Language-Action architecture that internally generates visual primitives to guide robotic manipulation. This approach enables the Vision-Language Model to explicitly provide spatial targets to the action expert, resulting in a 27.61% higher success rate on complex Chinese chess manipulation tasks and enhanced generalization to novel scenarios.

hot.title: Spatial Memory for Out-of-Vision Manipulation in Vision-Language-Action
hot.summary: SOMA, a framework for Vision-Language-Action models, integrates a persistent spatial memory constructed from multi-view observations to enable robust robotic manipulation of objects initially or temporarily outside the camera's field of view. The approach yielded improved success rates across five real-world out-of-vision tasks, reducing target localization time by 40-59% and head search path length by 40-57%, while also achieving state-of-the-art performance in fully observable simulation benchmarks.

likes.title: Process Reward Models That Think
likes.summary: This research introduces THINKPRM, a generative process reward model that enables large language models to provide verbalized, long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification for their reasoning steps. The model, developed by a collaboration including University of Michigan and LG AI Research, achieves high performance with orders of magnitude less step-level supervision than traditional discriminative models, while significantly improving reliability and generalizability.

likes.title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report
likes.summary: Microsoft Research introduces BitNet b1.58 2B4T, the first open-source, natively trained 1-bit Large Language Model at the 2-billion parameter scale, pre-trained on 4 trillion tokens. This model achieves competitive performance with full-precision LLMs of similar size while requiring substantially less memory (0.4 GB), exhibiting lower decoding latency (29 ms), and consuming significantly less energy.

likes.title: A Survey on Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models: What, How,  Where, and How Well?
likes.summary: A comprehensive survey introduces a unified, four-axis taxonomy to systematically organize the rapidly growing field of Test-Time Scaling (TTS) in Large Language Models (LLMs). This work provides a structured framework for classifying methods, offers practical guidelines for deployment, and identifies critical open challenges for future research in enhancing LLM performance during inference.

likes.title: Scaling Laws for Native Multimodal Models
likes.summary: Researchers at Apple conducted a comprehensive study on scaling laws for native multimodal models, demonstrating that early-fusion architectures trained from scratch can achieve comparable performance to late-fusion approaches while offering superior training efficiency and lower deployment costs. Integrating Mixture of Experts into these early-fusion designs further enhances performance and enables implicit specialization to different modalities.

likes.title: Why do LLMs attend to the first token?
likes.summary: Large Language Models learn attention sinks, often directed at the first token, as a fundamental mechanism to prevent information degradation, known as over-mixing and representational collapse, which is crucial for maintaining performance, particularly in processing long contexts. Removing these sinks at inference time severely impacts model utility across various tasks.

likes.title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
likes.summary: This paper introduces 'sleep-time compute,' a method for optimizing Large Language Model inference by pre-computing insights about persistent contexts during idle periods. The approach reduces test-time compute by approximately 5 times for similar accuracy on reasoning tasks and decreases average query cost by up to 2.5 times when amortized across multiple queries over the same context.

likes.title: Vision as LoRA
likes.summary: Vision as LoRA (VoRA), developed by ByteDance, proposes an encoder-free architecture for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by internalizing vision capabilities directly into LLMs using mergeable LoRA layers. This approach achieves performance comparable to encoder-based models with near-zero additional inference cost and supports arbitrary image resolutions, all while demonstrating stable and data-efficient training through block-wise distillation and bi-directional attention for vision.

likes.title: Frame Context Packing and Drift Prevention in Next-Frame-Prediction Video Diffusion Models
likes.summary: FramePack introduces a framework for next-frame-prediction video diffusion models, employing progressive context packing to manage memory and novel anti-drifting sampling strategies. This system enables the generation of thousands of coherent video frames while maintaining visual quality and mitigating the accumulation of errors.

likes.title: Real AI Agents with Fake Memories: Fatal Context Manipulation Attacks on Web3 Agents
likes.summary: A study by Princeton University and the Sentient Foundation formalized "memory injection" as a stealthy context manipulation attack against LLM-powered Web3 agents. The research empirically demonstrated that these attacks achieve higher success rates than prompt injection and bypass current prompt-level defenses, with fine-tuning showing improved robustness, particularly on the CrAIBench benchmark and ElizaOS.

likes.title: Holistic Fusion: Task- and Setup-Agnostic Robot Localization and State  Estimation with Factor Graphs
likes.summary: A factor graph-based framework enables task-agnostic robot state estimation by jointly optimizing local and global states while automatically aligning multiple reference frames, demonstrating real-time performance across diverse platforms (ANYmal, RACER, HEAP) and environments while handling sensor drift through random walk modeling.

likes.title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
likes.summary: NVIDIA researchers developed GR00T N1, an open foundation Vision-Language-Action model for generalist humanoid robots. The model achieves robust performance on real GR-1 humanoid robots and simulation tasks, utilizing a 'data pyramid' strategy for efficient training and strong generalization across diverse robot embodiments and scenarios.

likes.title: Kimi-VL Technical Report
likes.summary: Kimi-VL is an efficient open-source Mixture-of-Experts vision-language model that achieves competitive performance across diverse multimodal tasks, often matching or exceeding larger proprietary and open-source models with only 2.8 billion activated parameters. Its "Thinking" variants enhance reasoning, while the architecture supports 128K extended context and native-resolution visual inputs.

likes.title: I-Con: A Unifying Framework for Representation Learning
likes.summary: Researchers at MIT, Google, and Microsoft developed I-Con, an information-theoretic framework that unifies over 23 diverse machine learning loss functions, including those for dimensionality reduction, contrastive learning, and supervised learning, under a single KL-divergence objective. This unified perspective enabled the creation of new debiasing strategies and a novel unsupervised clustering method, "Debiased InfoNCE Clustering," which achieved state-of-the-art performance on ImageNet-1K with gains of up to 7.8% in Hungarian accuracy.

likes.title: It's All Connected: A Journey Through Test-Time Memorization,  Attentional Bias, Retention, and Online Optimization
likes.summary: A unified framework from Google Research introduces "Miras" for sequence modeling that reinterprets attention mechanisms and forgetting gates as forms of memory optimization, leading to three new architectures (Moneta, Yaad, and Memora) that demonstrate improved performance on language modeling and recall-intensive tasks while providing theoretical insights into existing models.

likes.title: SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models
likes.summary: Hugging Face and Stanford researchers develop SmolVLM, a family of compact multimodal models that process both images and videos while requiring less than 1GB of GPU memory for the smallest 256M parameter variant, achieving competitive performance through optimized architecture design and training strategies that specifically target resource-constrained environments.

likes.title: SPRING: Systematic Profiling of Randomly Interconnected Neural Networks  Generated by HLS
likes.summary: Northwestern University researchers develop SPRING, a profiling framework for FPGA-based streaming machine learning accelerators that enables concurrent monitoring of over 200 internal signals while maintaining synchronization with data streams, integrated into the hls4ml open-source tool for automated analysis of randomly interconnected neural networks.

likes.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
likes.summary: This paper introduces MAST, an empirically derived taxonomy of 14 multi-agent system failure modes, and MAST-Data, a dataset of 1642 annotated execution traces. The work reveals that failures in multi-agent LLM systems primarily stem from system design issues and inter-agent misalignment, rather than solely from underlying large language model limitations.

likes.title: Describe Anything: Detailed Localized Image and Video Captioning
likes.summary: NVIDIA and UC Berkeley researchers introduce DAM (Describe Anything Model), a vision-language architecture that generates detailed captions for specific regions in images and videos through a focal prompt mechanism and localized vision backbone, achieving state-of-the-art performance across 7 benchmarks while addressing data scarcity through a semi-supervised learning pipeline.

likes.title: Multi-Token Attention
likes.summary: Researchers at FAIR, Meta, introduced Multi-Token Attention, an architectural modification that enables LLMs to condition attention weights on multiple query and key vectors simultaneously, improving long-context information retrieval and general language understanding with minimal parameter overhead.

likes.title: InternVL3: Exploring Advanced Training and Test-Time Recipes for  Open-Source Multimodal Models
likes.summary: InternVL3 establishes a new native multimodal pre-training paradigm for MLLMs, allowing the model to jointly acquire visual and linguistic capabilities from the outset. This approach achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models, reaching 72.2 on the MMMU benchmark, and demonstrates strong competitiveness with leading proprietary models across a wide range of multimodal tasks.
